title: Built a neon survival shooter with ChatGPT connected to a real dev machine
author: LuozhuZhang
selftext:
We built a small game called **NEON SWARM** — a top-down neon shooter where you survive 60 seconds of enemy waves.

We used **Open Machine (OM)**, our open-source, local-first MCP runtime, to connect ChatGPT to our actual development environment.

[https://github.com/OpenMachineLabs/openmachine](https://github.com/OpenMachineLabs/openmachine)

Here's the workflow:

1. Built the game in TypeScript + Canvas, with movement, auto-shooting, enemies, and particle effects.
2. Ran builds and automated tests directly on the machine.
3. Opened the game in Chrome and tested the gameplay, including a full 60-second win and Game Over.
4. Fixed bugs found during review, passed 60 tests, and merged the GitHub PR after CI passed.

What's interesting about OM is that it connects AI to real project files, terminals, browser workflows, and GitHub, with scoped permissions and persistent execution records.

It's still a small experiment, but the entire game development workflow happened on a real machine.

The game and source code are [open source](https://github.com/OpenMachineLabs/neon-swarm-demo).

Curious how others are integrating AI into their game development workflows.
